basic_details.job_title: APSSB Group C Recruitment 2026 Notification Out – Apply Online for 217 Constable Driver, Driver, Pharmacist and More Posts

content_sections.text: Vacancies are as reported by the departments and may change. content_sections.heading: How to Apply for APSSB Group C 2026
content_sections.text: Apply only online at apssb.nic.in between 21 October (3:00 PM) and 5 November 2026 (5:00 PM). Applications by any other mode are rejected. Enter the details of one photo identity document (Aadhaar, Voter ID, driving licence, PAN or another Government photo ID). The same document in original must be carried to the exam with the admit card, and the name and father's name on it must match the admit card. Mark your preference of posts and departments . You can mark preferences only against posts you are eligible for, and the order is final; the merit list is drawn as per the preference order you give. Upload: scanned signature on white paper in black ink (10–50 KB, JPG/JPEG/PNG); recent passport-size photograph (50–100 KB, JPG/JPEG/PNG); and copies of the educational and technical certificates relevant to the posts applied for. PwBD or PwD candidates needing a scribe or compensatory time must opt for it in the form and upload the relevant Annexure (I, IA, II or IIA from the APSSB Candidates Corner). Pay Rs. 150 online and submit. Check every entry before submitting; details cannot be edited after the closing date, and incomplete or junk entries are rejected. If you submit more than one form for the same post, only the latest counts. Download the admit card from apssb.nic.in when released; no admit card is posted individually.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process and Exam Pattern
content_sections.text: Minimum 33% in each paper separately ; no sectional cut-off within the Common Paper. No negative marking. Technical papers: Paper 1 ANM; 2 Laboratory Technician; 3 Pharmacist; 4 ECG Technician; 5 Dental Technician; 6 Health Assistant Jr.; Paper 7 (Road Safety and Traffic Signages) for all five driver and constable posts ; 8 Field Publicity Assistant; 9 Publicity Assistant. Syllabus: Common Paper notified under No. APSSB-13/9/2026/1437 and Technical Papers under No. 1438, both dated 8 October 2026, in the Syllabus section of apssb.nic.in. No re-evaluation or re-checking of answer scripts. The Board may withdraw questions. PST/PET: candidates shortlisted at 1:8 of vacancies on written-exam merit, subject to 33% in each paper. Ex-servicemen are exempt from the PET but must pass the PST. Driving test: shortlisted at 1:3 , subject to 33% in each paper and, for Head Constable Driver, clearing PST/PET. ANM competency test: shortlisted at 1:3 . Four stations of 5 minutes and 10 marks each (vital signs; maternal and child health; infection control protocol; basic procedure in midwifery), qualifying 7 marks per station. Each candidate takes three of the four stations and must score 21 out of 30 . Medical fitness test for the three police and fire-service driver posts. Stages II to V are qualifying only. Final merit is on written-examination marks alone. Provisionally shortlisted candidates upload, then produce in original with self-attested copies: two photographs; Matriculation certificate for date of birth; educational, technical and registration certificates; experience certificates; APST certificate; PRC; PwBD certificate; NOC from the head of department for serving Government employees; discharge book and PPO for ex-servicemen; admit card and application printout. A claim not made in the application form is not considered from the certificates, and no extra time is given to produce documents. Biometric checks are used against impersonation.

content_sections.heading: Exam Centre and Conduct
content_sections.text: The examination is held in the Itanagar Capital Region . The Board may cancel a venue or divert candidates; no change of date, time or centre is accepted. Calculators, laptops, mobile phones, watches and other electronic devices are banned; possession leads to debarment and legal proceedings, and centres have no storage. Scribe and 20 minutes per hour compensatory time are available to eligible PwBD/PwD candidates who opt for them in the application; a candidate's own scribe must be one qualification step below the candidate and may not be a candidate in this examination.

faq.question: Q1. Can candidates from outside Arunachal Pradesh apply?
faq.answer: No. Under the Uniform Eligibility Criterion applied to all vacancies, every candidate must hold an APST certificate and a Permanent Residence Certificate of Arunachal Pradesh and speak an indigenous tribal language of the State. The UR vacancies are the unreserved share within that pool.

faq.question: Q2. Is there negative marking?
faq.answer: No. Candidates must score at least 33% in the Common Paper and 33% in the Technical Paper separately; there is no sectional cut-off inside the Common Paper.

faq.question: Q3. What is the fee?
faq.answer: Rs. 150, paid online, non-refundable. PwD and PwBD candidates pay nothing.

faq.question: Q4. Can I apply for more than one post?
faq.answer: You indicate preferences for all posts and departments you are eligible for in the application, in an order that cannot be changed later; the merit list follows that order. If you submit more than one form for the same post, only the latest is considered.

faq.question: Q5. Where is the exam held?
faq.answer: In the Itanagar Capital Region, tentatively on Sunday, 29 November 2026. Centre and date changes are not entertained.

faq.question: Q6. How is the final merit decided?
faq.answer: On written-examination marks only. The physical, driving, competency and medical stages are qualifying and do not add marks.

faq.question: Q7. What is the ANM competency test?
faq.answer: A practical test of four stations (vital signs; maternal and child health; infection control protocol; basic midwifery procedure), 5 minutes and 10 marks each with 7 marks qualifying. Each candidate attempts three stations and must score 21 of 30. Candidates are called at 1:3 of vacancies.
